sentences.text:
Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C ) has been filed by petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no.0102/2017, registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC ) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Rajat Aneja and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Loveleen from Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 04.08.2013 and out of this wedlock one female child was born.

On the basis of a complaint lodged by respondent no. 2, present FIR bearing no. 0102/2017 was registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC against petitioners.

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have been living together for the last three years along with the minor child.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.
8. It is stated that one of the terms of settlement mentioned at para 7 of the Settlement Agreement dated 30.01.2023 has not been complied with.
However, petitioner no. 2 who is present in the Court, who is mother of petitioner no. 1, states that the condition will be complied with on or before 24.05.2023.
9. The complainant, who is present alongwith her counsel, states that she has no objection to the same.

10. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

11. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 0102/2017, registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
